title: "You can actually resolve them": UFO expert Avi Loeb says his new telescope will solve problems related to high-resolution UAP images
excerpt: UFO expert and professor at Harvard University Avi Loeb claimed that his new telescope could solve issues related to high-resolution UAP images.
content:
UFO expert and professor at Harvard University Avi Loeb claimed that his new telescope could solve issues related to high-resolution UAP images. While speaking to NewsNation's Blake Burman, the professor said,

"If you have a large telescope, let's say a meter-scale telescope, and you point it at the direction of these mysterious orbs, you can actually resolve them and figure out what they are."

Loeb added,

"But you can also take a spectrum and figure out their composition. And so I came up with a concept where a radar system would monitor the sky."

Loeb went to the Pentagon on November 12, 2026, to pitch a new sensor system for studying UAP. The expert explained that scientists would build a prototype astronomical telescope in Ithaca, New York, with $1.5 million in funding. After testing and deploying this device, Loeb's team planned to place identical tracking systems in areas where military personnel frequently spot UFOs.

Continue reading more about UFO's HD image capture process with Avi Loeb's new telescope.

Avi Loeb claimed his meter-scale telescope could capture HD UAP images

While having a discussion with Blake Burman regarding the UFO tracking system, Avi Loeb said that he found pretty revealing answers from the president. The professor pointed out that Trump's remarks sounded very familiar because he already has that exact same knowledge. Loeb clarified that he had never seen any mysterious, giant, silver, alien spacecraft after certain individuals claimed that the U.S. government had those things. He even suggested that it might not even exist.

Loeb revealed that these reported mysterious and glowing orbs were also spotted by both FBI agents and personnel from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence. He said,

"When orbs were reported, these are mysterious spherical balls of light that are seen by FBI agents, by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence people."

The professor explained that his team needed a high-resolution image of the UAP to solve the puzzle behind these strange sightings. He said that it's only possible by using a meter-scale telescope. Loeb explained that if the telescope could be pointed in the direction of these mysterious orbs, one could actually resolve them and figure out what they were.

Loeb explained plans to put the instruments in military locations where UFOs had been spotted

Loeb shared plans to build a meter-scale telescope that would be trained on those military areas where UFOs had been spotted. The professor explained that these telescopes would help individuals to gather high-resolution images and other information related to UFOs. Loeb said,

"We are starting to order the parts now. And once we test it and employ it, we can then put the same instruments in locations where military personnel are seeing objects they cannot identify."

Loeb said that one could also take a spectrum and figure out the composition of these orbs with the help of the telescopes. Therefore, he came up with a concept where a radar system would monitor the sky. He said if the radar noticed some unusual object, it would steer that telescope in the object's direction.
